jobs.prompt:
Write a NEW real-pipeline test, tests/dispatch-integrate-real.test.mjs. This is a test-only ticket: do not change any production code in tools/. Read tests/field-lesson-t80-cli.test.mjs in full as context first - it already exercises the real `runManifest` (exported from tools/swarm.mjs) against a real fixture project with an injectable `spawnImpl`, and shows the real claude-CLI JSON-result protocol its existing `fakeSpawn()` helper emits (an in-process EventEmitter fake). Your job builds on the SAME real `runManifest`/`integrateRun` (both exported from tools/swarm.mjs - read their exported signatures directly in that file, do not guess) and the SAME fixture-project setup style (tmpdir, real `git init`, a real context file committed), but replaces the in-process `fakeSpawn()` EventEmitter fake with a REAL spawned OS child process: a small, hermetic fake-agent Node script, written to a temp file at test setup, spawned via a real `spawnImpl` you inject into `runManifest` (e.g. `spawnImpl: (cmd, args, opts) => spawn(process.execPath, [fakeAgentScriptPath, ...controlArgsForThisScenario], opts)` - the real `node:child_process` `spawn`, not a fake). The fake-agent script is a genuine separate process with its own real exit code, its own real stdout buffering, spawned detached in its own process group.

Read tools/swarm/core-41.mjs's real dispatch spawn call as context (search for `spawnImpl(job.agent`): it spawns differently for `job.agent === 'claude'` (using `claudeArgs(job, {resume})` from tools/swarm/core-1.mjs, with `env: process.env`) versus any OTHER agent name (using `extraCliArgs(job)`/`extraCliEnvironment(job.agent)` - the generic/hermes-shaped CLI path, a DIFFERENT env-construction path). Your test must cover BOTH paths - at least one scenario with `job.agent: 'claude'` and at least one with a different agent name (e.g. `job.agent: 'hermes'` or similar, matching whatever `extraCliArgs`/`extraCliEnvironment` actually expect - read their real signatures in tools/swarm/core-41.mjs/core-1.mjs to get this right, do not invent a shape that does not match). This matters because a real regression was just found where a normal process exit completed before the 'close' event fired, failing every CLI-shaped worker (both paths) - your test is the regression guard for that class of bug, at the full pipeline level (spawn through integrate), not a dispatcher-unit-level test (a separate ticket, tests/dispatcher-output-capture.test.mjs, covers the dispatcher unit itself with real children - do not duplicate that, yours proves the WHOLE pipeline works end to end, spawn to integrate).

Write the fake-agent script to emit a REAL claude-CLI-shaped JSON result line on real stdout (matching the exact shape tests/field-lesson-t80-cli.test.mjs's existing `fakeSpawn()` emits - read it for the exact field names: `type`, `subtype`, `is_error`, `result`, `total_cost_usd`, `permission_denials`), then exit with a real exit code - the script's exact behavior is controlled per-scenario via an argv flag or env var you design (document it in a comment), so one script file serves every scenario below rather than five separate scripts.

Scenarios, each run through the REAL `runManifest`+`integrateRun` pipeline, not a dispatcher-only unit test:

(a) Success with large stdout: the fake agent writes over 300 KB of non-result text to stdout BEFORE its final result JSON line, and the exit event fires only after all of that stdout has been written and read (a real ordering concern, not simulated) - assert the run completes `ok`, the full declared output file lands correctly in the fixture project after `integrateRun`, and the captured stdout length recorded by the run (if the run state exposes it) reflects the real captured size, not a truncated one.

(b) Exit code 3 with stderr: the fake agent writes something to real stderr and exits with real code 3, writing no valid result line at all. Assert the job/run status is recorded as failed, the REAL exit code (3, an actual number, not null) and the stderr content are recorded in the run state, and NOTHING from this job is integrated (declared output files must not appear in the fixture project tree).

(c) Job timeout: the fake agent sleeps past the job's configured timeout and never exits on its own. Assert the run reports a timeout status, whatever partial stdout had been produced is kept/recorded, the child is actually killed (verify no process with that pid group remains alive after the test - do not just trust the status field, actually check `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws ESRCH or equivalent after teardown), and clean up defensively in `t.after` regardless (kill the process group if anything is still alive, for test-leak hygiene).

(d) Two-job manifest, one fails one succeeds: in a single manifest with two jobs, one scenario-(b)-shaped (fails) and one scenario-(a)-or-plain-success-shaped (succeeds), assert the failing job does not prevent or hide the succeeding job's own success and its own file correctly integrating.

(e) Worker token presence (REQUIRED, the mechanism is on this branch): the dispatcher in tools/swarm/core-41.mjs issues a worker token for local CLI agents that can run the guard hook (claude, claudeShell, codex, cursor) and puts it in the child's environment under the name SWARM_WORKER_TOKEN (read the real code and tools/worker-token.mjs for the exact name and helper functions). Have the fake-agent script write `Object.keys(process.env)` (key NAMES only, never any value) into its result output, and assert: for a `job.agent: 'claude'` job the key SWARM_WORKER_TOKEN is present; for a hermes-shaped job it is ABSENT; the token never appears in argv, in the run state, or in any stored output (scan the saved run folder for the token value, which the TEST obtains by reading it in the fake agent ONLY as a hash: the fake agent writes the sha256 of the value, never the value, and the test compares that hash against the hash recorded in the worker token record under the swarm runs folder while the job runs or via the helper in tools/worker-token.mjs); and after the job ends the token record is revoked (use the real revoke or verify function from tools/worker-token.mjs to assert the token no longer verifies).

(f) Real git-integration check: after a successful scenario's `integrateRun`, assert BOTH that the output file's real content on disk matches exactly what the fake agent produced, AND that the resulting git state (working tree diff, or the integrate commit if one is made - check how tests/field-lesson-t80-cli.test.mjs or tests/board-card-ui.test.mjs-adjacent integrate tests verify this, follow the established pattern) contains EXACTLY the declared output file and nothing extra (no stray temp files, no unrelated changes).

Leak hygiene (required for every scenario that spawns a real child): per-test timeout of 60000 ms or less (use node:test's own `{ timeout: ... }` option, not a manual setTimeout race); every real child spawned detached in its own process group (`detached: true` on POSIX, matching the real dispatcher's own `detached: process.platform !== 'win32'` convention from core-41.mjs); explicit kill of the process group in `t.after` for every test, even ones expected to exit cleanly on their own (defense against a future bug leaving one hanging) - use a negative pid (`process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGKILL')`) to kill the whole group, matching how this codebase's own `terminateProcessGroup`-style helpers do it elsewhere (search tools/self-manage/watchdog.mjs for the pattern, read-only, do not import from it, just match the convention).

Run the test file when done and confirm every scenario passes for real (not just that it doesn't throw) before reporting complete. IMPORTANT: secret scanner: never write credential-looking literals.
